question: Did the city of Ai exist after Joshua destroyed it?
summary: Joshua 8:28 says Joshua burned Ai and made it "an heap for ever, even a desolation unto this day," but Nehemiah 7:32 lists 123 men of Bethel and Ai among those returning from Babylonian exile — meaning a populated Ai existed roughly a thousand years later.

reconcile.connective: Defenders read Joshua's "for ever" as the Hebrew idiom for "a long time," which leaves room for Ai's ruins to be resettled by the time of the return from Babylon.

discrepancy.connective: The objection is pressed at face value by Steve Wells, who lists Joshua's permanent "desolation unto this day" against a populated Ai among the post-exilic returnees roughly a thousand years later.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Did the city of Ai exist after Joshua destroyed it?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/ai.html)

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Joshua 8:28
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this exact pair at Joshua 8:28: he glosses 'an heap for ever' as 'for a long time' and explicitly grants that Ai 'appears to have been rebuilt, and to have been inhabited by the Jews, after their return from their Babylonish captivity, Neh 11:31' — the row-surfaced harmonizing commentator keyed to the passage (Haley's specific coverage of this pair unconfirmed).

link.title: Defending Inerrancy: Nehemiah 7:32 — If Ai was destroyed earlier, why is it still inhabited here?

excerpts.excerpt_text: and made it an heap for ever; that is, for a long time, for it appears to have been rebuilt, and to have been inhabited by the Jews, after their return from their Babylonish captivity, Neh 11:31 …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: The only gathered note that names BOTH poles of the tension at once — it reads Joshua's 'for ever' as 'a long time' AND concedes Ai was rebuilt and inhabited after the Babylonian captivity, the exact post-exilic Ai the Nehemiah list presupposes. Single strongest on-tension reconcile. Truncated mid-sentence (source continues ', even a desolation unto this day') → ' …'.
excerpts.source_note_text:
And Joshua burnt Ai,.... The whole city, fire being only set before to a few houses, to make a smoke as a signal; he did with it as he had done with Jericho, for so he was ordered, Jos 8:2,
and made it an heap for ever; that is, for a long time, for it appears to have been rebuilt, and to have been inhabited by the Jews, after their return from their Babylonish captivity, Neh 11:31,
even a desolation unto this day; to the time of the writing of this book; and by what has been just observed, it appears that Ezra could not be the writer of it, since this city was inhabited in his time.
